judgments.reason: The 2014 paper applies EEG performance estimation to baseline simulated driving and a perceptual discrimination task. The Mind Wandering dataset extends the Baseline Driving paradigm and is not this paper's data.
judgments.paper_title: Estimating endogenous changes in task performance from EEG

judgments.reason: Brooks & Kerick 2015 studies alpha ERSP and steering corrections in a driving task, topically related to BCIT driving data but not describing the Mind Wandering dataset itself.
judgments.paper_title: Event-related alpha perturbations related to the scaling of steering wheel corrections

judgments.reason: Garcia et al. 2017 analyzes EEG-behavior directionality in driving, likely from BCIT driving data; it does not introduce the Mind Wandering dataset (audio and vigilance task).
judgments.paper_title: Estimating direction in brain-behavior interactions: Proactive and reactive brain states in driving
